title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: draft typescript of Grothendieck's 1970 Barsotti–Tate/crystal material, close to the ICM Nice talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' and the Montréal lectures. It has been filed in the Gauss–Manin/Cartier dossier.

The previous page sets up the problem. Let S_0 be a scheme of characteristic p and G_0 a Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) group over S_0. The contravariant Dieudonné crystal D*(G_0) is an F-V-crystal on the crystalline site of S_0. It recovers the fibres of G_0 at perfect points. Problème 1 asks whether D* is fully faithful, and whether its essential image consists of the 'admissible' F-V-crystals. Grothendieck thinks that solving it requires a Dieudonné theory for finite locally free p-group schemes, at least those flat over Λ_n = Z/p^n. Such a theory would use extra structure, probably a filtration on an object of a derived category, which a marginal note says is 'sans doute inutile si S_0 est parfait'.

This page states Problème 2: develop such a theory for finite locally free p-groups over a base S_0 of characteristic p > 0.
- If S_0 is perfect, establish an anti-equivalence between two categories.
- On one side: finite locally free group schemes over S_0 that are flat as sheaves of Z/p^n-modules (essentially level-n truncated objects, e.g. kernels G[p^n] of BT groups).
- On the other side: locally free W_n(O_S)-modules M with Frobenius-semilinear F_M and Frobenius^{-1}-semilinear V_M satisfying FV = VF = p.

Grothendieck observes that a positive answer to Problème 2 would imply Problème 1 for perfect S_0. The reason is that a BT group is the system of its G[p^n], and over a perfect base the crystal is just a W(O_S)-module with F and V.

The next page goes on to the Hodge filtration ω_G ⊂ D*(G)_S.
errors: 'car.p 0' should read 'car. p > 0' (the symbol is missing in the typescript); this is not a mathematical error.

The 'conditions habituelles' are not spelled out. The intended conditions are FV = VF = p, with F semilinear for the Witt-vector Frobenius σ and V σ^{-1}-semilinear (σ is bijective since S_0 is perfect).

A gap rather than an error: the requirement that M be locally free over W_n(O_S) matches groups flat over Z/p^n. A Dieudonné theory for all finite locally free p-groups over a perfect base needs W(O_S)-modules of projective dimension ≤ 1, not locally free W_n-modules. Grothendieck restricts to the flat case, which avoids the problem.

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of the crystalline Dieudonné functor on BT groups over a characteristic-p base, and description of its essential image ('admissible' F-V-crystals)
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of crystalline Dieudonné theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Posed by Grothendieck (ICM 1970). Partial solutions: Berthelot–Breen–Messing (1982); de Jong (1995, bases with local p-bases / formally smooth); de Jong–Messing; Lau and others for further cases
ideas.where_published: ICM Nice 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

ideas.what: Over a perfect base, anti-equivalence between finite locally free p-groups flat over Z/p^n and locally free W_n(O_S)-modules with F, V
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné theory over perfect rings/schemes (classification of truncated BT groups and finite flat group schemes by Dieudonné modules)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (1980, perfect valuation rings); Gabber (unpublished, perfect rings); Lau (2013/2018, written proofs, semiperfect/perfectoid extensions)
ideas.where_published: Possibly listed among the problems in the Montréal notes or the ICM text; not certain of the exact wording

ideas.what: A Dieudonné theory over general characteristic-p bases needs extra structure, probably a filtration on an object of a derived category
ideas.modern_name: Precursor of filtered/derived Dieudonné theories (Breuil–Kisin-type and prismatic Dieudonné theory, Anschütz–Le Bras; derived Hodge filtration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later work: Fontaine, Breuil, Kisin, Lau, Anschütz–Le Bras, Bhatt–Scholze
ideas.where_published: Hinted at in the Montréal lectures; mainly on the previous page

deep.surprise_reason: Both problems belong to Grothendieck's well-known 1970 Dieudonné-theory program, as stated at the ICM and in the Montréal lectures. The perfect-base case was later settled by Gabber and Lau, with Berthelot's earlier case of perfect valuation rings. Nothing here is absent from the record.
